RFC3748-2-1.note: TestRFC3748AuthenticatorLockStep counts outstanding Requests in a local variable it increments and decrements itself, so its checks cannot fail; it proves only that each authenticator call returns one packet, which the *Packet return type already guarantees.

RFC3748-2-2.note: TestRFC3748AuthenticatorRequiresValidResponse: the negative arm feeds a Code-1 packet and asserts an EAP-Failure, which the RFC does not ask for; the case the sentence is about, an INVALID Response (wrong Identifier or Type) drawing no new Request, is not under this id.

RFC3748-2.1-1.note: Clauses: peer uses one method; authenticator uses one method. Authenticator clause: TestRFC3748OneMethodPerConversation feeds a Type-13 Response once MS-CHAPv2 is active and fails on out != nil or auth.Succeeded(). Peer clause: no assertion in this unit shows the peer refusing to run a second method (that behaviour is tagged under RFC3748-2.1-4 only), so a peer that switched methods stays green here.

RFC3748-2.1-2.note: Clauses: one method per conversation; the authenticator then sends Success or Failure. The second is asserted (TestRFC3748MethodCompletionSendsResult: last.Code != CodeSuccess on a good password, fail.Code != CodeFailure and Succeeded() on a bad one). The one-method clause of the quoted span has no assertion in this unit: it is tagged under RFC3748-2.1-1.

RFC3748-2.1-3.note: Forbidden: a peer answering a Request with a legacy or expanded Nak after its first non-Nak Response. TestRFC3748PeerNaksBeforeItCommitsToAMethod negative: after commitment a Type-40 Request must be Discarded and fails on res.Response != nil (any Response, so both Nak forms) or res.Err. Positive: before commitment the same Type-40 Request draws a legacy Nak naming MS-CHAPv2 (wantLegacyNak), so the discard is tied to commitment.

RFC3748-2.1-4.note: Clauses: the authenticator MUST NOT send a Request of a different Type before the final round; MUST NOT send a Request for an additional method; a peer receiving such Requests MUST silently discard them. Only the peer clause is asserted (TestPeerDiscardsARequestOfAnotherType fails on !res.Discarded, res.Err, res.Response for a Type-13 Request after MS-CHAPv2; TestPeerProcessesARequestOfTheMethodType fails if a method-Type Request is discarded). Neither authenticator MUST NOT has an assertion: an eap.Session that emitted a Request of another Type mid-method stays green.

RFC3748-2.2-1.note: Clauses: Success, Failure, Nak Response, Notification Request, Notification Response carry no data for other methods. Asserted: a Nak Response is never handed to the method (len(rec.seen)/len(tap.seen) != 0 fails), Success/Failure encode to 4 octets (len(wire) != 4 fails), the peer's Notification Response has empty Type-Data. The Notification Request clause has no assertion (the authenticator emits none, and no {single-polarity} or scope marker says so). The two tagged functions are near-duplicates.

RFC3748-4-1.note: Clauses: a Length larger than the received octets; the message MUST be silently discarded. TestRFC3748PacketLengthDiscard asserts only DecodePacket returns an error on a 5-octet packet declaring 12. Silence is not asserted: nothing shows the caller that receives the decode error sends nothing and keeps the conversation, so a caller answering with EAP-Failure or ending the SA stays green.

RFC3748-4-2.note: Clause: the Length field counts Code, Identifier, Length and Data. Asserted: a Success encodes to 4 octets and decodes; 3-octet input and a declared Length of 3 are refused. No assertion reads the Length field Ze encodes, and no decode case distinguishes a Length that counts the header from one that counts Data only, so an encoder writing len(Data) into Length on a Request with Data stays green.

RFC3748-4-4.note: Forbidden: padding beyond Length reaching the packet or refusing it. TestRFC3748LengthBoundsTypeData fails on a decode error or TypeData != "abc" for a packet with 3 trailing octets. Both tags sit on the same padded input and the same assertions (the negative is a second check of the positive's result), so there is one test, not a pair, and the row carries no {single-polarity} marker.

RFC3748-4-5.note: Clauses: authenticator discards Codes other than 1-4; peer discards them. Authenticator: Codes 0,5,6,255 fail on out != nil, and the next Identity Response must still open MS-CHAPv2. Peer: eapdWantDiscarded on each undefined Code, then the Identity Request must still draw an Identity Response. Positive: defined Codes 1,3,4 draw a Failure from the authenticator (out == nil fails) and the peer answers a Request and returns ErrEAPFailure on Failure.

RFC3748-4.1-1.note: TestRFC3748PeerHasNoRetransmitTimer asserts only that the peer answers each Request (responses > 0). Neither clause can fail it: no case hands the peer an invalid Request to show no Response is sent, and the no-timer clause rests on the synchronous API, not an assertion.

RFC3748-4.1-11.note: Clauses: Response Type matches or is a Nak; a peer MUST NOT Nak after an initial non-Nak Response. The tagged units assert the authenticator discarding a Response of another Type (TestAuthenticatorDiscardsAResponseOfAnotherType) and processing one of the method Type. The quoted Type rule binds the Response sender, and the Nak-after-non-Nak clause has no assertion under this id (proved under RFC3748-2.1-3).

RFC3748-4.1-3.note: TestRFC3748NewRequestChangesIdentifier proves every new Request changes the Identifier; the first clause of the quoted span, a retransmitted Request keeps the same Identifier, has no case under this id.

RFC3748-4.1-4.note: Forbidden: a peer Response whose Identifier differs from the outstanding Request's. TestRFC3748ResponseEchoesRequestIdentifier fails on resp.Identifier != requests[i].Identifier for every Response of a full MS-CHAPv2 flight, and on an unusual Identifier 0xC3 not echoed (catches a peer that counts or uses a constant).

RFC3748-4.1-5.note: Clauses: the Response Type matches the Request; or it is a Nak for an unacceptable Type. Clause 1: resp.Type != requests[i].Type fails over the flight. Clause 2 and the forbidden case (answering an unacceptable Type with a non-Nak): a Type-99 Request fails on res.Err, no Response, Response.Type != TypeNAK, or Type-Data != [MS-CHAPv2].

RFC3748-4.2-1.note: {single-polarity: positive} carried on the row. Forbidden: the authenticator re-sending Success or Failure. TestRFC3748SuccessFailureNotRetransmitted fails on a non-nil packet from Process after a Failure (Nak path) and after a Success (full MS-CHAPv2 flight).

RFC3748-4.2-11.note: Clauses: Success and Failure may be lost; the peer MUST allow for this. Asserted for a lost Success only: the peer does not conclude before it, discards stray packets without ending the session, and concludes on the late Success. A lost Failure has no case, so a peer that could not survive a missing EAP-Failure stays green.

RFC3748-4.2-15.note: Clauses: the peer terminates and indicates failure; MUST silently discard Success (the Failure discard is a MAY). Termination: the EAP-Failure fails unless res.Err is ErrEAPFailure. Success discard: a later Success fails on !Discarded, Done, a non-zero MSK or Succeeded(). Positive: a completed peer concludes on the Success (Done false or Discarded fails).

RFC3748-4.2-2.note: TestRFC3748SuccessFailureFormat positive proves Success/Failure encode to 4 octets with no Type; the negative arm refuses a 4-octet Request, a neighbouring rule (Requests carry a Type). No case under this id hands Encode a Success carrying Type-Data and asserts it is dropped.

RFC3748-4.2-4.note: {single-polarity: positive} carried on the row (sender obligation). Forbidden: a Success or Failure whose Identifier is not the answered Response's. out.Identifier != responseID fails on the refused-code Failure (0x42), the Nak Failure (0x7E), the identity-stage Failure (0x11) and the Done-method Success (0x5A).

RFC3748-4.2-5.note: Clauses: on unsuccessful completion, triggered either by the authenticator's failure result indication or by the peer deciding not to continue, the peer terminates and indicates failure. Asserted only for an authenticator-refused exchange (peerFinal.Err not ErrEAPFailure or Done fails). The peer-decides trigger (for example a bad Authenticator Response) has no assertion in this unit.

RFC3748-4.2-6.note: Forbidden: the waiting peer silently discarding the Success or the Failure. Success: peerFinal.Done false or an all-zero MSK fails. Failure: peerFinal.Err nil or Done true fails. Both packets of the quoted 'either of them' are covered.

RFC3748-4.2-7.note: Forbidden: acting on a Success sent at connection. A Success on a fresh peer fails on eapdWantDiscarded, on Succeeded(), and if the following Identity Request is no longer answered. Positive: the same Success at method end must conclude Done with a non-zero MSK.

RFC3748-4.2-8.note: Clauses: an unpermitted Success is discarded; an unpermitted Failure is discarded. Only Success is asserted (mid-MS-CHAPv2 Success fails eapdWantDiscarded and Succeeded(); the permitted Success later concludes). No unit hands the peer an unpermitted Failure, so a peer that ended the session on it stays green.

RFC3748-5-1.note: Forbidden: a Request of Type 3 or 254. Every Request of a full MS-CHAPv2 flight fails on req.Type == TypeNAK or TypeExpandedEAP; a Nak Response, the input a faulty authenticator would echo, must draw a Failure (out.Code != CodeFailure fails).

RFC3748-5.2-1.note: Forbidden: no Notification Response to a Notification Request (the prohibiting-method exception applies to no method Ze runs). wantNotificationResponse fails in the identity state, on a 4000-octet message, on a zero-length and a non-UTF-8 message, and res.Discarded fails; the identity exchange must continue afterwards.

RFC3748-5.2-2.note: Forbidden: a Nak answering a Notification Request. wantNotificationResponse (Type 2 Response) fails on each malformed Notification Request; the same peer Naks a Type-40 Request (Response.Type != TypeNAK fails) and then answers a Notification with a Notification Response, so the Notification path is distinguished from the Nak path.

RFC3748-5.3.1-4.note: Forbidden: a Nak used as an error indication. A truncated MS-CHAPv2 Challenge must return the method error with no Response (res.Response != nil fails, so no Nak carries it); control: the same peer Naks an unacceptable Type 40 (wantLegacyNak).

RFC3748-5.4-1.note: Positive: an MD5-Challenge Request draws a Type-4 Response with the Request Identifier and the independently computed MD5 value. The negative tag (Identity Requery discarded) exercises the Section 2.1 rule, a neighbouring one, and the row carries no {single-polarity} marker, so the pair is incomplete.

RFC3748-5.4-2.note: Sentence: EAP peer and EAP server implementations MUST support MD5-Challenge. Positive TestRFC3748MD5ChallengeSupportedByBothRoles goes red if either role cannot run Type 4 (res.Response nil, no CodeSuccess, peer not Done). The negative TestRFC3748MD5ChallengeIsTheConfiguredMethod proves a neighbouring rule (Type 4 is only answered when configured), not a violation of the support obligation, and the row carries no single-polarity marker, so the pair is incomplete.

RFC3748-7.10-1.note: Clauses: MSK of at least 64 octets; EMSK of at least 64 octets. TestRFC3748MSKSize checks len(MSK)==64 (fixed by the [64]byte type) and not all-zero, so an MSK with only its first octets derived stays green. The EMSK clause of the quote has no assertion here (tagged under RFC3748-7.10-2, which quotes the same sentence).

RFC3748-7.10-2.note: Clauses: MSK of at least 64 octets; EMSK of at least 64 octets. EMSK: len != 64, all-zero, ends differing, and the exact TLS export octets 64-127 or the HKDF expansion are asserted for EAP-TLS and MS-CHAPv2. MSK: only emsk != MSK and all-zero on refusal are asserted, so an MSK with a short derived prefix stays green.

RFC3748-7.10-4.note: Sentence: key-deriving methods MUST provide mutual authentication. Peer-authenticates-server is proven: an untrusted server cert must not let the peer conclude or derive an MSK. Server-authenticates-peer is only shown by len(serverState().PeerCertificates)>0 on a trusted exchange; no unit presents an unverifiable client certificate and asserts the server refuses. EAP-MSCHAPv2, also key-deriving in ze (eap_mschapv2.go derives an MSK), is not covered.

RFC3748-7.10-6.note: rfc3748_emsk_test.go and rfc3748_mschapv2_emsk_test.go prove the EMSK is held by both ends, erased on Close, and absent from both MSKs and every wire packet. The last clause, 'or used to derive any other keys', is unproven: an MSK derived by hashing the EMSK would pass the byte search.

RFC3748-7.10-7.note: Forbidden: an exchange that fails when one party discarded key state the other still holds. With the authenticator's ticket keys discarded and a peer offering the stale ticket, resumption on either side fails the test (lines 67, 70) and the new MSK must differ from the kept-state MSK; control: with the state kept, both sides resume (lines 48, 51).

RFC3748-7.5-1.note: Sentence: peers, authentication servers and authenticators not in pass-through MUST validate a per-packet MIC. Negative runTamperedEAPTLS corrupts only authenticator-to-peer Requests, so only the peer clause goes red (the peer-concluded Fatal). No unit tampers a peer Response, so the authentication-server clause has no assertion.
